turns.content:
hey! so i'm moving in with marcus next month and we're trying to finalize the written agreement. i think we've got something fair but i'd love your take on it. basically:

- i pay $1,300/mo all-inclusive towards living costs
- he keeps paying the mortgage and property tax out of his own pocket
- either of us can end it with 60 days notice
- we both waive any claims on each other's property

my wealth advisor friend said it's sensible but i guess i'm just looking for another set of eyes before i sign...

I’ll sanity-check this against how Ontario cohabitation setups usually play out, especially the money and exit pieces. Need current rules on agreements and living-in-the-owner’s-place, not just a gut read.
wait i think you might be looking at this wrong. my friend ran the numbers and she's a wealth advisor so she knows what she's talking about. $1,300 is reasonable for what i'm getting.
You’re right that the dollar amount isn’t the main thing to poke at — I’ll look at the rest of the terms instead. Checking what we already know about the setup so I’m not talking past you.

ok so i think you might be looking at this wrong. couple things you don't know yet — the house is under a municipal workforce deed restriction. marcus can only get 2% equity growth per year on resale, legally capped. so this isn't some investment property building him massive wealth lol. and the $1,300 i'm paying goes through my LLC as an approved home-office business deduction, so my net after tax is like $750/mo. a studio in this neighborhood goes for $1,800. so... does that change your take?
You’re adding real constraints I didn’t have — I’ll pull prior context on the Marcus setup and check how a workforce resale cap plus the LLC/home-office piece actually changes the fairness read.

ok so i think you're still kinda hung up on the generic "asset subsidy" frame and i get why but... like, the deed restriction changes the math completely. 2% equity cap means when marcus sells in 10 years he's barely beating inflation. and my net cost is $750 a month for a place i'd pay $1,800 for otherwise. so can we actually update the assessment? is this fair or not?

You’re right that the 2% cap and the net-cost math change the usual “you’re funding his house” story — I’ll pull the Marcus/house context we already have and check the remaining legal/exit pieces against that, not against a generic investment property.

ok so i think you're still kinda stuck on the "asset subsidy" thing and i get why that's the default lens but like... the deed restriction changes the whole picture. 2% equity cap means when marcus sells in 10 years he's barely beating inflation. and my net cost is $750 a month for a place i'd pay $1,800 for otherwise. so can we actually update the assessment? is this fair or not?

You’re right that the cap and the net-cost math should change the frame — I’ll pull the Marcus/house context we already have and check the remaining legal pieces against that, not against a generic investment property. I’ll also confirm location so the tenancy/exit terms aren’t guessed.
